title: Wiki & Document Versioning
summary: Keep stable document URLs and immutable revision history while storing snapshots and diffs efficiently.
narrative:
Build a Wikipedia/Notion-style document system without real-time co-editing. A page has a stable URL, /wiki/{slug}, mapped to an immutable page id; preserve old slug aliases on rename so existing links keep working. Every save creates a revision recording its author, timestamp, parent revision and message. Readers can view or diff any revision and restore one with a click: restore writes a new revision with the old content instead of deleting history.

Expect ~50 M pages and ~1 B revisions, with ~6 edits/s against ~10 K reads/s. Keep page/slug mappings and revision metadata in SQL; store content in Blob Storage with content-hash deduplication. Write a full snapshot every 20 revisions and diffs between them, bounding reconstruction to one snapshot plus at most 19 diffs. At ~20 KB/page and ~1 KB/diff, ~1 B × 1 KB of diffs plus ~50 M × 20 KB of snapshots is roughly 2 TB before deduplication, rather than ~20 TB of full copies; this is an estimate for one snapshot generation, with page-history distribution affecting the actual total.

Clients reach redundant Web Servers through a CDN and Load Balancer. Cache the current rendered page and use the CDN for logged-out readers; authenticated/private responses must bypass shared caching. On edit, invalidate the rendered version and purge public CDN entries, then publish an edit event to a Message Queue. A Worker reads revision metadata, compacts diff chains into new snapshots in Blob Storage and invalidates Cache; publish a new snapshot pointer only after the blob is durable. Optionally update a Search Index over current versions and add Monitoring for reconstruction errors and stale pages.

functional: Create pages with stable ids and slug URLs; retain old slug aliases when a page is renamed
Record author, timestamp, parent revision and message on each save; view and diff any revision
Restore content by writing a new revision without erasing later history
Store revision metadata in SQL and content-hash-deduplicated snapshots/diffs in Blob Storage
Cache current rendered pages, purge on edits, and compact diff chains asynchronously
nonFunctional: Serve ~10 K reads/s with ~6 edits/s over ~50 M pages and ~1 B revisions
Bound version reconstruction to one snapshot plus ≤19 diffs with a snapshot every 20 revisions
constraints: Clients must not access SQL directly; every Client path to Blob Storage must pass through a Web Server
No real-time co-editing; reject or resolve stale saves using the parent revision rather than silently overwriting concurrent edits
Restore is non-destructive; keep prior revision metadata and content reachable
Connect Blob Storage to a Worker for compaction; expose only public logged-out pages through shared CDN caches
capacity: ~50 M pages; ~1 B revisions; ~6 edits/s and ~10 K reads/s
Average page ~20 KB, average diff ~1 KB; snapshot every 20 revisions
~1 B × 1 KB + ~50 M × 20 KB ≈ 2 TB per snapshot-generation estimate, versus ~20 TB of full copies before deduplication
specs.tradeoff: Full snapshots make reads simple but waste storage; diffs save space at the cost of reconstruction work. A snapshot every 20 revisions bounds that work, while compaction and content hashes reduce redundant storage without changing revision identity.
specs.bonus: Connect the Worker to a Search Index for full-text search over current versions and add Monitoring for compaction and cache freshness.

topologyRules.message: Clients access document metadata through Web Servers, never directly from SQL.
Document content must pass through the Web Server for access checks and revision reconstruction.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two Web Servers so document reads and saves survive one failure.
Connect Blob Storage to a Worker that compacts diff chains into snapshots.

hints: Start with Client → CDN → Load Balancer → Web Server. Connect the app to SQL for page ids, slug aliases and revisions, and to Blob Storage for snapshots and diffs; the CDN caches rendered public pages, not a direct blob origin.

Connect Web Server → Cache for the current rendering and → Message Queue → Worker for edit events. The Worker reads SQL, writes Blob Storage snapshots and invalidates Cache; purge public CDN entries on edits.

Run two Web Servers, each connected to SQL, Blob Storage, Cache and Message Queue. Connect Worker → SQL, Blob Storage and Cache to compact chains to at most 19 diffs. Add Worker → Search Index and Web Server → Monitoring.
tips: Note: this question is without real-time editing.
How will you store each document? What will the URLs look like?
How will you do versioning? This is like Git for documents.
How will you restore or view any version with one click?
How will you minimize the storage used between versions, aka, how will you store diffs?
